OOHDASH-159 design rev 4 · all screens, today vs proposed · 29 Oct 2026

Rev 4: the text key applied to every screen

Every screen in every journey (184 states), captured from today's release (v1.6.5) and from a working copy of rev 4, both run locally on test data. Open a screen to see today on the left and rev 4 on the right, with each piece of text tagged by its type. 178 screens change. The decisions behind this are in the gate document and the earlier analysis page (oohdash-159-text-key.html).

The key
  • Script: green "🗣 Say to the customer" box, one per step. A question to the customer is its last line.
  • For you: blue box for background, with values from the site highlighted.
  • Ticket text: dashed box, "📄 What goes on the ticket".
  • Warning: red, directly above every button that logs a ticket or switches equipment. A P1 gets a solid red heading and a red "Raise the P1" button.
  • After-action card: neutral, dark header with the ticket number, the same for every outcome.
  • What we know so far: 👤 customer answers and 🔎 dashboard checks only. Also written onto the ticket.
Good places to start
  • Show: "Only screens 159 changes"
  • Journey: "OOHDASH-159 kitchen scenarios" (scenario 1 = K159-s1, 2 = K159-s2, 3 = K159-s3)
  • Site page (the connection-check banner is gone; the controls panel is fixed)
  • Device control window (the warning above Send)
  • Text type: "Script: unlabelled grey quote" (present today, none left in rev 4)

Every screen, every piece of text

Each screen is the app's own output, captured from today's release (v1.6.5) and from the proposed 159 code. Open a screen to see it as rendered (with optional type labels) and each piece of text with its type and any problem flagged (⚑). Problem flags: 431 pieces of text today.

How this was captured

Pub heating is click-walked separately on each version, so its screens are listed as "Pub heating (boiler panel)" (today) and "Pub heating (rev 4 walk)".

  • Today's release (main 2ab9486 / v1.6.5, the live image) and the proposed 159 code (rev 3 working copy, the same one the prototype was built from) were each run locally in test-data mode. A script drove every journey into each state and tagged every piece of text by the style it actually uses on screen.
  • The journey states come from the OOHDASH-146 screen dump: 110 states across all flows, the control window and the other screens. Added for this review: the 159 kitchen scenarios (sites 8889, 8888 and 6750), the site page states, and a click-walk of pub heating at sites 9010 and 9011.
  • Some states use injected test data where no test site has that condition; each is marked in its note. Ticket numbers and times come from test data.
  • Not covered: admin screens, pop-up toasts, and some timer-banner states. These are listed so nothing is assumed covered.
  • Production was only read: one read of the deployment settings and logs. Nothing was changed.
